title: AI supply chains: from a capable model to economic value
status: Round1 B1/B2 and optional P1/P2 author repairs applied; independent round2 pending

sections.teaching_construction: A successful service still needs a feasible production plan

claim_provenance.claim: Stipulated service unit, planning period, asset/organization graphs and economic decision

sections.teaching_construction: 1. Identify the economic outcome before estimating an effect

claim_provenance.claim: Unit cost, labor productivity, profit and counterfactual effects measure different objects
Dated customer-support sample, issues-resolved-per-hour outcome and heterogeneous estimated effects; identification depends on the stated observational design
claim_provenance.origin: Generative AI at Work, retained April 2023/November 2023 revision, PDF pages 1–2, 4–5 and 15–16; not randomized assignment or an aggregate employment/wage estimate

sections.teaching_construction: 2. A benchmark measures a task; a firm chooses a strategy

claim_provenance.claim: Benchmark equality does not determine price, cost, strategy or vertical integration
claim_provenance.origin: Recording concepts with original matched-quality comparison

sections.teaching_construction: 3. Track assets and organizations in parallel

claim_provenance.claim: Technical assets and organizational supply/control relations are separate graphs
claim_provenance.origin: Recording distinction with original responsibility table

sections.teaching_construction: 4. A serial capacity constraint cannot be repaired at the wrong stage

claim_provenance.claim: Ideal steady-state serial flow equals minimum compatible stage capacity
Nonbinding-stage and tied-bottleneck improvements

sections.teaching_construction: 5. Data acquisition creates costs and obligations through different transactions

claim_provenance.claim: Acquisition method, access, rights, quality and costs differ
Conditional per-work arithmetic does not identify license price or legal outcome
claim_provenance.origin: Original stipulated division; no recorded settlement certification

sections.teaching_construction: 6. Distribution determines feasible applications before it determines costs

claim_provenance.claim: Release access changes feasible applications and operational obligations
claim_provenance.origin: Recording distinctions with original service contract

claim_provenance.claim: Linear serving-cost crossover and parallel-line cases
5000crossover and10000costs under matched quality/capacity assumptions

sections.teaching_construction: 7. A forecast needs a quantity, horizon and mechanism

claim_provenance.claim: Level changes and constant per-period rates require a measure and horizon
Repeated constant-rate recurrence gives compounded multiplier

sections.teaching_construction: 8. Translate task savings through explicit exposure and adoption

claim_provenance.claim: The cited task framework distinguishes exposure, economic adoption, cost savings, TFP and GDP; the main ten-year exercise excludes a broad scientific-discovery transformation
claim_provenance.origin: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI, retained May 2024 working paper, PDF pages 1–3 and 5–7; description of the cited model's scope

claim_provenance.claim: Reported conditional ten-year model estimates: baseline at most roughly 0.66% TFP; revised assumptions give 0.53% TFP and 0.90% GDP upper bounds; these are not realized outcomes or annual rates
claim_provenance.origin: The Simple Macroeconomics of AI, retained May 2024 working paper, PDF pages 2–3 and 5–7; values and scenario qualifications checked against the original, without reproducing its full general-equilibrium computation or proof

claim_provenance.claim: Fixed task-cost partition gives weighted exposure/adoption/net-savings identity and convex bound
claim_provenance.origin: Original accounting proof; not Hulten/general-equilibrium theorem

claim_provenance.claim: Exposed/adopted/saving product exact 207/31250
claim_provenance.origin: Recomputed PDF page 6 inputs; precision is arithmetic only

sections.teaching_construction: 9. Complementary investment separates invention from realized productivity

claim_provenance.claim: General-purpose-technology criteria comprise pervasiveness, continuing technical improvement and downstream innovation complementarities
claim_provenance.origin: General Purpose Technologies: Engines of Growth?, retained August 1992 working paper, PDF pages 1–2; conceptual criteria from the original abstract, not the later journal edition

claim_provenance.claim: The productivity J-curve names a conditional measurement framework involving intangible investment and later capital services; the framework does not impose a universal time pattern
claim_provenance.origin: The Productivity J-Curve, retained October 2018/January 2020 revision, PDF pages 1–5 and 13–14; description of the cited framework and explicit pattern limitation, without reproducing its full growth-accounting derivation

claim_provenance.claim: Signed additive wedge examples illustrate sign changes without universal trajectory
claim_provenance.origin: Original illustration; not published TFP formula

sections.teaching_construction: 10. Output accounting and consumer value measure different objects

claim_provenance.claim: Ad-funded provider output in GDP differs from consumer welfare; the separate digital-economy-estimate omission statement refers to the August 2020 vintage
claim_provenance.origin: BEA FAQ 1250, complete retained article; official accounting explanation with its stated estimate vintage, not a new estimate of free-service welfare

claim_provenance.claim: Nominal/real/per-capita measures and WTP/WTA differ
Conditional 100-user monthly-10 annual-12000 example
claim_provenance.origin: Original stipulated extrapolation; recorded empirical survey not adopted

sections.teaching_construction: 11. Choose aggregation weights before summing sector effects

claim_provenance.claim: Fixed normalized sector shares give convex bounds
Value-added telescoping and gross-output ratios sum7/5
claim_provenance.origin: Original two-stage ledger; no network productivity theorem

sections.teaching_construction: 12. Constant returns does not mean equal optimal input allocations

claim_provenance.claim: Joint homogeneity and unique interior Cobb–Douglas budget optimum under stated positive domains
claim_provenance.origin: Original algebra, logarithmic derivative and concavity proof

claim_provenance.claim: Unequal allocation fourth powers27versus16

sections.teaching_construction: 13. More productive work and faster idea production are different growth mechanisms

claim_provenance.claim: Nonrival reuse differs from production cost and access
Specified multiplicative/additive idea recurrences have different level/growth paths
claim_provenance.origin: Original iteration; no Romer-model or empirical-growth certification

sections.teaching_construction: 14. Identify the measurement that would change the decision

claim_provenance.claim: Recorded forecast/resource assessments remain qualified judgments
claim_provenance.origin: Recording discussion; no verified current national bottleneck

claim_provenance.claim: Decision-specific measurements and causal/aggregation requirements

Actual stdout/snippet,9755reference assertions andPEP8pass

claim_provenance.claim: Worked serial-flow, cost, savings, allocation and recurrence reasoning under stated models
Capacity, double-counting and growth counterexamples
Dated paper versions, original constructions and unsupported empirical quantities distinguished
